evals.prompt: We have an existing React/Tailwind app with shadcn-style primitives, scattered raw colors, light/dark mode, and no design docs. Establish a design architecture without replacing our stack or generating lots of documentation.
evals.expected_output: Inspects existing tokens/components first, preserves coherent conventions, proposes a minimal .design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md and decisions log, consolidates semantic theme roles, and identifies high-leverage architectural fixes rather than creating a new component library.

evals.prompt: Audit this dashboard UI architecture. I suspect engineers have started making local copies of buttons and using raw hex colors. Prioritize what matters instead of giving me a cosmetic review.
evals.expected_output: Findings are severity-ranked, distinguish system violations from polish, focus on duplicated canonical controls and semantic-token bypasses, and propose root-level corrections before local styling fixes.

evals.prompt: We need a split button for Publish with a dropdown for Publish and archive / Schedule. Should I create a new component? Apply our design-system architecture and tell me what to change.
evals.expected_output: Searches existing button/menu primitives, reasons from semantic and keyboard behavior, prefers composition or a justified reusable component rather than visual duplication, defines states/focus/error behavior, and updates project documentation only if the shared contract changes.

evals.prompt: Review a dense desktop-first document manager for engineers: file tree, search, table, review status, comments, version history, keyboard shortcuts, and light/dark themes. We want long-session usability, not a sparse marketing-dashboard aesthetic.
evals.expected_output: Preserves useful density, evaluates scanning/comparison and workflow context before decoration, checks power-user navigation and state visibility, enforces semantic tokens/components/themes, and includes keyboard/focus/accessibility without automatically enlarging or card-ifying the interface.
